publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: A description is given of the causes of voltage sags in industrial plants, their impact on equipment operation, and possible solutions. The definition proposed focuses on system faults as the major cause of voltage sags. The sensitivity of different types of industrial equipment, including adjustable speed drive controls, programmable logic controllers, and motor contactors, is analyzed. Available methods of power conditioning for sensitive equipment are also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of df/dt in power system protection and its implementation in microcontroller based intelligent load shedding relay
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: Several practical intelligent setting schemes that consider the effect of df/dt are suggested and simulated for a power system operating in an underfrequency situation. Considerations for df/dt relay setting are discussed. These intelligent setting schemes have made a positive improvement in the underfrequency condition. As an extension of these new intelligent control schemes, a microcontroller based intelligent under/over frequency relay is introduced. With its advanced hardware and intelligent software, this microcontroller has the advantages of high flexibility, less cost, and high communication ability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of standards limiting harmonic distortion in power systems
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: Harmonic distortion in power systems is growing due to the popularity of switch-mode power electronic equipment. This electronic equipment has recognized advantages, including reducing weight and improving control and efficiency in power converters and supplies. A disadvantage of switch-mode power electronic equipment is that the low-cost utility interface design approach may burden the power system with harmonic loading. Methods to reduce this distortion exist but economic incentives do not. Standards are emerging as the most effective means to influence equipment design and control distortion in power systems. This work compares the major European and American harmonic limiting standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A k-step predictive scheme for speed control of diesel driven power-plants
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: An adaptive speed control scheme for diesel prime-movers is presented. Diesel prime-movers are characterized by nonlinear, time-varying parameters, including a nonlinear input dead-time variation that introduces an unknown delay between the injection of fuel and the production of engine torque. Such plants are difficult to control by conventional proportional-integral (PI) controllers. It is shown that by assuming the existence of an additional system time-constant, an explicit estimate of the plant parameters and dead-time can be obtained. The algorithm converges quickly. The resulting predictor can then be used to set up a k-step-ahead predictive controller. Studies are presented to compare the performance of the adaptive scheme to that of a fixed, tuned PI controller. The algorithm is shown to be flexible enough to operate under a wide range of droop settings, and equally applicable to various operating conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of DC ripple and commutation on the line harmonics of current-controlled AC/DC converters
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: Line harmonics are usually predetermined under the simplified assumption that the DC current is sufficiently smoothed. But in practical operation of controlled converters, e.g., feeding medium-size DC drives, the DC ripple often cannot be neglected. For the predetermination of line harmonics this means that the operating point is specified by the EMF (electromotive force) and the mean value of the DC current, i.e., the associated control and commutation angles are unknown. The consideration of the basic effects of commutation and DC ripple leads to line current harmonics separated into positive and negative sequence systems. Selected results of systematic evaluations show the amplitude and phase as a function of DC reactance as well as of the EMF and mean DC current in the range of usual low and medium-voltage supply networks. In comparison with the conventional precalculations, assuming sufficient DC smoothing, significant deviations occur in the case of higher DC ripple.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: All amperes are not created equal-a comparison of current ratings of high-voltage circuit breakers rated according to ANSI and IEC standards
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: The internationalization of the electrical power equipment market has required engineers to apply equipment designed and built to unfamiliar standards. For high voltage circuit breakers, the two best known standards are the ANSI and IEC standards. Since ratings with similar names have different meanings in the two series of standards, it is vital that application engineers understand the differences. The continuous current, interrupting, short-time and closing current ratings are examined, and these ratings in the two series of standards are compared.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A range of directly connected TCRs to reduce voltage disturbances
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: A description is presented of a range of thyristor values which have been produced for direct connection to supply systems at up to 38 kV, thus obviating the need for a step down transformer at these voltages. A number of examples illustrate these two systems and their applications to the compensation of pulsed loads, arc furnaces, mine winders and both conventional and cyclo-convertor fed steel mill drives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: For a successful ASD installation . . .look beyond the electronics
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: Electrical and mechanical design of drive components must suit wiring practices based on recognized industry standards. Safety grounding, medium voltage cable termination, cable training, and electrical clearances are discussed using power plant fan installations in a particular power plant as a case study. The design shortcomings found during the installation of several large 4 kV drives and the corrective actions taken (including the revision of specifications for later drive projects) are explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Proposed IEEE blue book-application guide for low voltage molded case circuit breakers and power circuit breakers
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: The P1015 Working Group of the IEEE Low Voltage Protection Subcommittee is preparing an application guide for low voltage circuit breakers used in industrial and commercial power systems, to be published as the IEEE Blue Book. The purpose of this guide is to provide information for selecting the proper circuit breaker for a particular application. This guide helps the application engineer specify the type of breaker, rating, trip functions, accessories, acceptance tests, and maintenance requirements. This guide also discusses circuit breakers for special-purpose applications; for example, thermal only, instantaneous only, and switches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: When a power supply system has a relatively low short circuit level, industrial loads such as arc furnaces, or converters for large motor drives, can cause voltage disturbances which may adversely affect other consumers. A description is presented of the development of a very simple static Vr compensator (SVC) of low rating designed for reducing such disturbances caused by loads up to about 10 MVA. A step down transformer is required and the small site area and simple design are ideally suited to industrial applications. The design of the SVC is described in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power quality of small rural industries
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: Results are presented of a detailed power quality survey of 23 small rural industries sponsored by the Canadian Electrical Association, and a knowledge base is provided on rural power quality and the possible origins of power supply anomalies. A summary is presented of the major power quality problems experienced at the various industrial sites. The results of the survey will provide a basis for promoting efforts by the utilities and their rural industrial customers to design and operate their electrical systems to minimize the effects of power supply anomalies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability of operation through proper specification of rotating machinery
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: The quality and extent of specifications developed for rotating electrical machinery will have a direct impact on the economic operation of all industrial facilities. This work provides an overview of how specifications can be developed for purchasing, operating, maintaining, and repairing large motors. The service life of all rotating machinery can be extended through a planned maintenance program that reflects operating conditions and the reliability desired. First cost versus operating cost can be optimized only when all factors in the industrial environment are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the significance of quality factor selection in harmonic filter design
publicationTitle: Conference Record. Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference 1991
abstract: Criteria for the design of harmonic filters to be inserted in low voltage electrical plants supplying static power converters, i.e., located in harmonic-polluted environments, are discussed. Particular attention is paid to the choice of the filter-inductor quality factor. The authors point out significant limits for the value of the quality factor which comply with the requirement of filter effectiveness in series resonance, limited harmonic amplification in parallel resonance and in the presence of supply-injected harmonic voltages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
